name: Liechtenstein
summary: Liechtenstein is in the EEA but keeps a quota on residence permits. EU/EEA citizens who work get permits from an annual quota (at least 56, half by lottery), and a separate small quota of 16 a year covers EEA citizens who live on their own capital. US and other citizens can only get a permit if they have a job or real economic significance for the country; residence cannot be bought. A lump-sum tax (25% of living costs) exists for new residents who do not work.
naturalisation: Not researched this session. Earlier practice: long residence (reported about 10 years) plus a municipal vote; not verified.
dual_citizenship_note: Not verified this session; Liechtenstein has generally required renunciation of other nationalities, with exceptions. See open questions.

routes.limited_places: a yearly quota of at least 56 permits, half by lottery
routes.name: EEA nationals: residence permit within the annual quota (employed)
routes.summary: EEA citizens with a job in Liechtenstein get residence from a yearly quota; the EEA agreement allows Liechtenstein to cap numbers, so there is no free right to move.
routes.requirements: Quota of at least 56 new residence permits a year for EEA nationals working in Liechtenstein, plus around 300 short-term permits (up to 12 months); half the long-term permits are allocated by the government on application and half by lottery (28 a year in the employed lottery). Swiss and UK nationals are not eligible for the EEA lottery; Swiss have their own channel of about 17 places.
routes.physical_presence: Residence in Liechtenstein for the permit

routes.limited_places: 16 permits a year for all EEA applicants (some sources say about 20)
routes.name: EEA nationals: quota permit without gainful activity
routes.summary: A small separate quota of 16 permits a year is open to EEA citizens who do not work and live on their own funds.
routes.requirements: Supplementary quota of 16 new permits a year for EEA nationals not exercising an economic activity (another source says about 20); sufficient own means. No numeric financial threshold published in the sources found. Applications compete for few places.

routes.name: Non-EEA nationals: permit for employment or economic significance
routes.summary: US and other citizens are admitted only in small numbers: with a job offer from a Liechtenstein employer or because they are of real economic significance to the country.
routes.requirements: Employment contract or real economic significance; limited annual permits. 'There is no direct purchase of residence through an investment' (private.law wiki). Exact quota numbers (one source claims about 89 a year) not confirmed.

routes.tax_note: Replaces ordinary income and wealth tax on a living-cost base; not an immigration permit.
routes.name: Lump-sum taxation for new residents
routes.summary: New residents who do not work in Liechtenstein can agree a tax of 25% of their worldwide living costs. It still needs a residence permit first.
routes.requirements: Tax Act arts. 30-33 as summarised by private.law wiki: not a Liechtenstein citizen, new to the country or back after at least 10 years away, no local gainful activity, living on foreign income or wealth. Amount agreed with the Fiscal Authority; no fixed minimum in the current Act.

open_questions: Official llv.li (Migration and Passport Office) pages returned 403; quota numbers come from an EU Commission review and secondary sources.
Government fees for permits not sourced.
Financial thresholds for the non-gainful EEA quota not published in sources found.
Years until permanent residence, naturalisation period and dual-citizenship rules not verified.
Lottery dates and exact split between lottery and government allocation are unconfirmed.
Lump-sum tax summary comes from a secondary wiki; statute not checked.
